questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Obligatory mobility; specialization theme with the professors of the University; cultural compatibility with the country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had all the information through email communication with both the host and sending universities.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: the mobility unit from the University of Padova helped us with information regarding covid rules, explaining the academic procedures and documents required in Italy

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I looked for it three months before my arrival and was lucky to find it through a Facebook group. However, I know many people who didn't find any accommodation for months and needed to stay in Airbnb, spending a lot of money. This is the most serious issue with the University of Padova I believe - there's no accomodation for this many students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very hard to find housing. Look for it way before your arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is through the University's website. All the explanation is provided by the mobility/welcome team.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The mobility/welcome team sent several emails to keep us informed and replied to questions via mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful, since they were all mandatory, I was automatically accepted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know how it works when classes are not mandatory.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Courses were focused more on practical issues for working in the area, which I found much more interesting than the courses from UCPH which were focused on academic and theoretical discussions.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Courses were focused more on practical issues for working in the area, which I found much more interesting than the courses from UCPH which were focused on academic and theoretical discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Environmental Resource Valuation; Forest Policy, Governance and Conflicts: from Global to Local; Market-based instruments for Economic Systems; Research Planning; Social Responsibility and Certification

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Thesis (Directed Studies and Final Examination)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: "Forest Policy, Governance and Conflicts: from Global to Local" is very interesting to learn how to analyse and assess policies and to learn methods for participatory strategies for working with groups. It requires a lot of time for preparing in between classes, but its very useful and interesting.

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing items, since I used a lot the facebook market trade or facebook groups of stuff donation, which are very common in Denmark, and in Italy that is not so common, so I needed to buy much more new things for housing/clothing than I did in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of festivals and concerts in spring and summer.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didnt participate in things organized by the University or other students. But here it is very easy to catch a train and go to beautiful and historical cities (Venice, Verona, Bologna, etc) and if you have a ride/car, to the mountains and the river.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Catch a train and go to beautiful and historical cities (Venice, Verona, Bologna, etc) and if you have a ride/car, to the mountains and the river.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Catch a train and go to beautiful and historical cities (Venice, Verona, Bologna, etc) and if you have a ride/car, to the mountains and the river.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I worked at a festival during the summer, which made me get to know a lot of local people (not only students).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are not as open here to integrate new people as they are in my country (Brazil), but way more than in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Political engagement, humor, food, history.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to find a place away from Padova in the summer. It gets REALLY hot in here and a desert city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look early for housing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To live in such a beautiful city and country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The thesis period was really lonely. Being an exchange student you don't know many people and going to the libraries by yourself to study during summer is hard. But I guess that's the same in every country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
